answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token stake before it may submit jobs or earn reputation. If later evidence shows coordinated identities were used to manipulate rankings, the protocol slashes their stakes and limits how quickly new accounts can gain influence. This creates a ridge of upfront cost: a sybil operator must fund many separate locks, while cheap hollow accounts cannot immediately steer outcomes. A ripple of detected abuse can also expose linked behavior, making the attacker risk losing funds across the cluster.
